title: Reverse Strings and Detect Palindromes
description:
Write a query that returns `id`, `word`, the `reversed` version of the word, and an `is_palindrome` flag (`'Yes'` if the word equals its reverse, `'No'` otherwise).

**Table: words**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| word | VARCHAR |
| category | VARCHAR |
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE words (id INT, word VARCHAR, category VARCHAR); INSERT INTO words VALUES (1, 'level', 'palindrome'), (2, 'hello', 'regular'), (3, 'racecar', 'palindrome'), (4, 'world', 'regular'), (5, 'madam', 'palindrome'), (6, 'python', 'regular'), (7, 'radar', 'palindrome');
solution_sql: SELECT id, word, REVERSE(word) AS reversed, CASE WHEN word = REVERSE(word) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS is_palindrome FROM words

test_cases.description: Returns 7 rows with reversed word and Yes/No palindrome flag

hints: `REVERSE(column)` returns the string with all characters in reverse order.
Combine `REVERSE` with a `CASE WHEN word = REVERSE(word)` to detect palindromes in a single query.
explanation: `REVERSE(word)` flips the characters. The `CASE WHEN word = REVERSE(word)` check identifies palindromes: level, racecar, madam, and radar all equal their reverse, so they get 'Yes'.
